correctness.rationale: For quasinilpotent B satisfying the explicitly quantified uniform superpolynomial resolvent-growth hypothesis, the exact cyclic polynomial resolvent identity T^m=diag(B) and norm comparison are valid. Root-of-unity Fourier inversion isolates each B-resolvent coordinate; the logarithmic small-power loss disappears under the hypothesis, giving the pointwise maximum exponent, its filtration, and the exact power set. The compact e^{-n^2} seed has polynomial lower bounds of arbitrarily high order, and interleaving unit links yields noncompact S with S^m compact and S^r noncompact for r<m. The B=0 case correctly limits the theorem. The [0,1] classification uses Ignatev Theorem 4 as an explicit external premise, not the finite checker.
